notesStmt.note: An early draft of lines for this poem (uva.00268) is written on the reverse of a letter to Whitman dated 14 August 1889. In his notes of a visit to the poet on 26 February 1890, Horace Traubel writes that Whitman reported "having sent 'A Twilight Song' to the Century." (See With Walt Whitman in Camden [Carbondale and Edwardsville: Southern Illinois University Press, 1982] 6:311). Therefore, the current manuscript must have been created between these two dates.

note.p: The faint note at the top of this manuscript indicates that it served as the printer's copy when the poem was published, with the subtitle "For unknown buried soldiers, North and South," in the May 1890 issue of Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine. With minor changes and without the subtitle, the poem was reprinted in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891) and in the "Good-Bye My Fancy" annex to Leaves of Grass (1891-1892).

lg.head: A Twilight Song
lg.l:
As I sit in twilight late alone by the flick⹀
eringflickering
oak⹀flame,

Musing on long-past war⹀scenes—of the countless
buried unknown soldiers

Of the vacant names, as unindented air's and
seas—the unreturn'd,

The brief truce after battle, with grim burial⹀
squads, and the deep⹀fill'd trenches

Of gather'd dead from all America, North, South,
East, West, whence they came up,

From wooded Maine, New England's farms, from
fertile Pennsylvania, Illinois, Ohio,

From the measureless West, Virginia, the South, the
Carolinas, Texas,

(Even here in my room⹀shadows and half⹀lights in
the noiseless flickering flames,

Again I see the stalwart ranks on⹀filing, rising—
I hear the rhythmic tramp of the armies;)

You million unwrit names, all, all—you dark
bequest from all the war,

A special verse for you—a flash of duty long neglected—
your mystic roll all‸strangely gather'd here,

Each name recall'd by me from out the darkness
and death's ashes,
To ‸Henceforth to be, deep, deep, within my thought recording ‸for many a future year here,
Your mystic roll ‸entire of unknown names or North or South,
Embalm'd with love in this twilight song.
